summary:
The U.S. has paused a major military campaign against Iran that could have lasted two weeks, officials said, as concerns grow over dwindling air defense stocks. Iran has ruled out talks and kept the Strait of Hormuz closed, escalating tensions that threaten global oil shipments. The pause gives room for diplomacy, but no new talks are scheduled.

Wildfires across France and Spain have forced hundreds of thousands to evacuate, burning over 42,000 hectares in Gironde alone and destroying 240 homes. The flames are threatening defense sites belonging to ArianeGroup, Dassault, and Thales, adding a strategic dimension to the disaster. Meanwhile, a shooting at a food festival near Seattle's Space Needle left three dead and several injured, including a two-year-old boy. Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson says a suspect is in custody.

China's chipmaking profits surged an extraordinary 2,579.5% in the first half of 2026, driven by AI demand, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Hong Kong exports followed suit, rising 53.4% in June to a record $81.7 billion — the largest monthly increase in 42 years. The numbers underscore how global AI spending is reshaping supply chains, with Chinese manufacturers and Hong Kong's ports at the center.

Ukraine's drone campaign in Crimea has cut power and water to towns, aiming to pressure Moscow into negotiations, though Russia has not acknowledged the crisis. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers set fire to mosques, cars, and farmland, Palestinians report, two days after a clash left four Palestinians and two Israelis dead. Uganda has begun emergency food relief in Karamoja after 19 died from hunger; 1.5 million people face acute malnutrition. And German police shot and killed the 21-year-old suspect who rammed a van into a Berlin Pride parade, ending a manhunt that began on July 26.

headlines.title: Trump Pauses Iran Strikes as Officials Weigh Dwindling Air Defense Stocks
headlines.summary: The U.S. paused a major military campaign against Iran that could have lasted two weeks, while Iran ruled out talks and kept the Strait of Hormuz closed, escalating tensions.

headlines.title: Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations in France and Spain, Threaten Bordeaux Defense Sites
headlines.summary: Hundreds of thousands evacuated as wildfires burn over 42,000 hectares in Gironde, France, destroying 240 homes and threatening ArianeGroup, Dassault, and Thales defense sites.

headlines.title: Three Dead, Several Injured in Shooting at Seattle Food Festival; Suspect in Custody
headlines.summary: A shooting at a food festival near Seattle's Space Needle left three dead and several injured, including a two-year-old boy. Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said a suspect is in custody.

headlines.title: China's Chipmaking Profits Surge 2,579% in First Half Amid AI Boom
headlines.summary: China's major chip manufacturers saw profits skyrocket 2,579.5% in H1 2026, driven by unprecedented AI demand and computing power needs, according to the National Bureau of Statistics.

headlines.title: Hong Kong Exports Soar 53% to Record $81.7 Billion in June on AI Demand
headlines.summary: Hong Kong exports surged 53.4% year-on-year in June to a record HK$641.1 billion ($81.7 billion), the largest monthly increase in 42 years, fueled by AI product demand.

headlines.title: Ukrainian Attacks in Crimea Deprive Towns of Power and Water
headlines.summary: Ukraine's drone campaign in Crimea caused power and water shortages for residents, aiming to pressure the Kremlin to negotiate. Moscow has not acknowledged the crisis.

headlines.title: Israeli Settlers Set Fire to Mosques, Cars, and Farmland in West Bank, Palestinians Say
headlines.summary: Palestinians report Israeli settlers torched mosques, cars, and farmland in the West Bank, two days after a clash that left four Palestinians and two Israelis dead.

headlines.title: Uganda Begins Emergency Food Handouts After 19 Die from Hunger in Karamoja
headlines.summary: Uganda launched emergency food relief in Karamoja after 19 died from hunger due to drought and crop failures, with 1.5 million people facing acute malnutrition.

headlines.title: Berlin Police Kill Suspect in Deadly Pride Parade Van Attack
headlines.summary: German police shot and killed the 21-year-old suspect who rammed a van into a Berlin Pride parade on July 26, killing one person and injuring 29 others, ending a manhunt.
headlines.previousContext: On July 26, a van rammed into a Berlin Pride parade, killing one and injuring 29; the suspect fled and was on the run until killed by police on July 27.
